content.toolsTag: A TOOLKIT THAT GETS OUT OF YOUR WAY
content.toolsText: These browser demonstrations use simulated actions. Your keyboard and screen are never captured.
cards: Readable keycaps, natural combinations and five renderers. Make the next step easy to follow.
Left click, right click and scroll direction — shown on a small indicator beside the pointer.
Move a separate magnified view of a selected screen area.
Make temporary notes, shapes and text over your screen while explaining an idea.

The verified preview hides displayed keys when protected input is detected. Detection has limitations and a known focus-notification race: hide the overlay manually before sensitive input. This is separate from trusting plugin code.
Appearance, saved profiles, input privacy and plugin management belong to the application. They are infrastructure, not separate plugins.

faq: What comes with the application?

Keys and mouse visualization are the two tools at the heart of Backpack. Keep your audience with you, one action at a time. Lens, Focus, Cursor magnifier, Timer — Plugin verified in package · Backpack 0.4.0-preview.4 / SDK 1.1. Drawing, Layout indicator — Plugin planned. Appearance, saved profiles, input privacy and plugin management belong to the application. They are infrastructure, not separate plugins.
Can I download Backpack or these plugins?

Backpack 0.4.0-preview.4 · Windows 10 / 11 x64. Public package not yet available Lens, Focus, Cursor magnifier, Timer — Plugin verified in package · Backpack 0.4.0-preview.4 / SDK 1.1. Drawing, Layout indicator — Plugin planned.
How are extensions installed and enabled?

In the verified preview: Plugins → Import a plugin → select .bppkg. Import validates and unpacks the package without running code or granting trust. A new or updated plugin starts disabled. First enable requires the application’s trust confirmation.
Are plugins isolated safely?

Install only from trusted sources. Plugins run in separate user-rights processes; that helps manage faults but is not a security sandbox. Manifest capabilities limit the Backpack interface, not everything the plugin can do on the computer.
Where do I start making a tool?

Start with the author’s presentation timer. A detailed guide with working examples will cover the contract, lifecycle, commands, settings, localization, building and .bppkg import. Current instructions are in F1 → Plugins. Public SDK/source links and updated SDK terms are being prepared.
Does key privacy protect every field?

No universal detection is promised. Protected and unknown input can be hidden, but asynchronous focus detection has limitations. Manually hide the overlay before sensitive input. Plugin trust is a separate decision.
Which systems and license apply?
The verified package targets Windows 10/11 x64 and includes .NET. Backpack is under PolyForm Strict 1.0.0; it is not open source. SDK terms are being updated for freely creating plugins.

model.developerText: Build tools freely for your own tasks. The author’s plugins show how Backpack can be extended, and a detailed step-by-step guide with working examples is being prepared.
developerSteps: The SDK connects a plugin’s start, stop and commands to Backpack. Commands can be assigned shortcuts.
The manifest describes settings; Backpack builds their controls and draws overlay panels. Panel colors are explicit parameters, not a promised automatic theme API.
Localized manifest labels and Context.Locale support the app’s languages. The included help explains the timer sample, building, packaging and .bppkg import.
model.docsNotice: In the application, open F1 → Plugins for the available contract, build and import instructions. Public SDK documentation and example-source links are not configured yet.
model.licenseNote: SDK terms are being updated to support freely creating your own plugins. The current package still uses its existing license; the updated terms, detailed build/import instructions and working examples are coming.
